newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: U.N. mission in Tajikistan renewed until June 15.
newsitem.headline: U.N. mission in Tajikistan renewed until June 15.

text.p: The Security Council unanimously approved on Friday a three-month renewal, until June 15, of a small U.N. observer mission in civil-war stricken Tajikistan, whose government and Islamic opposition last week signed a military agreement in Moscow.

The resolution welcomed the agreement, which sets out a plan to integrate the armed opposition into the army, and called it an important new step towards completing the task of national reconciliation. The accord followed a ceasefire last December which has largely held.
About 20,000 Russian-led troops fielded by the Commonwealth of Independent States (CIS) serve as border guards and internal peacekeepers in the remote mountainous republic.

The U.N. Mission of Observers in Tajikistan (UNMOT) has an authorised strength of about 45 observers, plus civilian support staff. But only about half a dozen observers and a handful of U.N. civilians remain in the country after most U.N. activities were suspended last month due to attacks by lawless elements, including several kidnapping incidents. Other U.N. personnel were relocated to Uzbekistan.
The council resolution strongly condemned the mistreatment of U.N. and other international personnel and called on all parties to cooperate in bringing the perpetrators to justice.

Secretary-General Kofi Annan was asked to report by April 30 on ways the United Nations might help in implementing the recent military agreement. Another report was requested by June 1 with recommendations on the U.N. presence in Tajikistan.
